title: Diplomatik til va yumshatish vositalari
goal_uz: Dars oxirida keskin fikr, iltimos, rad javobi va tanqidni diplomatik tarzda ifodalaysiz: sakkizta to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gapni yumshatish vositalari, bilvosita shakllar va obro‘ni saqlovchi iboralar yordamida qayta tuzasiz.

vocab.uz: fikrni ehtiyotkorlik bilan, kesin emas qilib aytmoq
zo‘rlab yuklash, birovni noqulay ahvolga solish

scenes.title: Diplomatik til darsiga xush kelibsiz
board: C2: Diplomatic Language
(Diplomatik til va yumshatish vositalari)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda grammatikaning nozik nuanslari va istisnolarini ko‘rdik: kichik bir so‘z ma’noni qanday o‘zgartirishini bildik. Bugun shu nozikligni muloqotga olib chiqamiz. Fikrni yumshatish, bilvosita iltimos va rad javobi, obro‘ni saqlash va tanqidni diplomatik aytishni o‘rganamiz. Dars oxirida sakkizta keskin gapni muloyim shaklga keltira olasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Today is about saying difficult things well: disagreeing, refusing and criticising without damaging the relationship.
scenes.say_uz: Yana xush kelibsiz. Bugun qiyin gaplarni yaxshi aytish haqida: munosabatga zarar yetkazmasdan e’tiroz bildirish, rad etish va tanqid qilish.

scenes.title: Nega diplomatiya kerak
board: Direct: That's wrong.
Diplomatic: I'm not sure that's quite right.
Same message, different relationship

examples.t: I'm not sure that's quite right.
examples.uz: Bu unchalik to‘g‘ri emasdir, deb o‘ylayman.

scenes.say_native: Diplomatik til yolg‘on emas. Xabar o‘zgarmaydi, faqat uning shakli suhbatdoshning izzatini saqlaydi. ‘That’s wrong’ va ‘I’m not sure that’s quite right’ bir xil fikrni bildiradi, lekin ikkinchisidan keyin hamkorlik davom etadi. Ingliz tilida, ayniqsa Britaniyada, ochiq keskinlik ko‘pincha qo‘pollik deb qabul qilinadi.
scenes.say: Diplomatic language is not dishonesty. The message stays the same; only the packaging changes, so that the other person can accept it without losing face.
scenes.say_uz: Diplomatik til yolg‘on emas. Xabar o‘sha-o‘sha qoladi, faqat qadoq o‘zgaradi, shunda suhbatdosh obro‘sini yo‘qotmay uni qabul qila oladi.

scenes.title: O‘zbek va ingliz nazokati
board: O‘zbek: siz, -lar, iltimos, malol kelmasa
English: modals, past tense, questions
✗ Give me the report. → ✓ Could you send me the report?

examples.t: Could you send me the report?

scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida hurmat asosan shakllar orqali bildiriladi: siz, ‘-lar’ qo‘shimchasi, ‘iltimos’, ‘malol kelmasa’, ‘-ib bersangiz’. Ingliz tilida ‘you’ hamma uchun bir xil, shuning uchun nazokat grammatikada yashaydi: modal fe’llar, o‘tgan zamon, savol shakli. Rus tilidagi ‘Дайте’ dan ta’sirlanib ‘Give me’ desangiz, inglizcha qo‘pol eshitiladi.
scenes.say: English has no polite form of you, so politeness lives in the grammar: modal verbs, past tenses and questions instead of commands.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida ‘you’ ning hurmat shakli yo‘q, shuning uchun nazokat grammatikada: modal fe’llar, o‘tgan zamon va buyruq o‘rniga savol.

scenes.title: Hedging: modal va fe’llar
board: might / could / may: This might cause delays.
seem / appear / tend to: It seems a little rushed.
I'd say… · I suspect… · I wonder if…

examples.t: This approach might cause some delays.
examples.uz: Bu yondashuv biroz kechikishlarga sabab bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.t: The deadline seems a little ambitious.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi mavzu: hedging, ya’ni fikrni qat’iy emas qilib aytish. Asosiy vositalar: might, could, may modal fe’llari; seem, appear, tend to fe’llari; ‘I’d say’, ‘I suspect’ kabi kirish iboralari. ‘This will cause delays’ o‘rniga ‘This might cause some delays’. Siz faktni inkor qilmayapsiz, faqat suhbatdoshga o‘ylash uchun joy qoldiryapsiz.
scenes.say: This will cause delays sounds like a verdict. This might cause some delays invites discussion. The deadline seems a little ambitious. I suspect we'll need more time.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Bu kechikishga olib keladi’ hukmdek eshitiladi. ‘Bu biroz kechikishga olib kelishi mumkin’ muhokamaga chorlaydi. Muddat biroz shoshilinchga o‘xshaydi. Menimcha, ko‘proq vaqt kerak bo‘ladi.

scenes.title: Yumshatuvchi so‘zlar
board: a bit / slightly / somewhat / a little
not entirely / not particularly
quite (BrE: fairly) · rather

examples.uz: Men to‘liq ishonch hosil qilganim yo‘q.

scenes.say_native: Yumshatuvchi so‘zlar gapning kuchini pasaytiradi: a bit, slightly, somewhat, a little. ‘It’s expensive’ o‘rniga ‘It’s a little on the expensive side’. Inkor bilan: ‘I’m not entirely convinced’, ‘not particularly helpful’. Diqqat: Britaniya ingliz tilida ‘quite good’ ko‘pincha ‘ancha yaxshi, lekin a’lo emas’ degani, Amerikada esa ko‘proq ‘juda yaxshi’ deb tushuniladi.
scenes.say: It's a little on the expensive side. I'm not entirely convinced. In British English, quite good often means fairly good, not very good.
scenes.say_uz: Bu biroz qimmatroq. Men to‘liq ishonmadim. Britaniya ingliz tilida quite good ko‘pincha ‘juda yaxshi’ emas, ‘ancha yaxshi’ degani.

scenes.title: Understatement: inkor + ijobiy sifat
board: bad → not ideal / not great
wrong → not quite right
boring → not the most exciting
scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilining sevimli usuli: salbiy so‘z o‘rniga ijobiy so‘zni inkor bilan aytish. ‘Bad’ o‘rniga ‘not ideal’, ‘wrong’ o‘rniga ‘not quite right’, ‘boring’ o‘rniga ‘not the most exciting’. O‘zbekchada ham ‘unchalik yaxshi emas’ deymiz, bu yerda ikki til o‘xshash. Farqi shundaki, inglizlar buni ancha ko‘p va hatto jiddiy muammolar haqida ham ishlatadi.
scenes.say: Instead of bad, say not ideal. Instead of wrong, not quite right. The timing isn't ideal can describe a serious problem very politely.
scenes.say_uz: Bad o‘rniga not ideal, wrong o‘rniga not quite right deng. ‘Vaqt unchalik qulay emas’ jiddiy muammoni ham juda muloyim tasvirlay oladi.

scenes.title: Zamon orqali masofa
board: I wonder → I was wondering
I hope → I was hoping
We think → We were thinking
I suggest → I would suggest

examples.t: I was wondering if we could talk.

scenes.say_native: Zamon va aspekt ham yumshatadi. ‘I was wondering’, ‘I was hoping’, ‘We were thinking’: o‘tgan zamon iltimosni hozirgi lahzadan uzoqlashtiradi, davomiy shakl esa uni taxminiyroq qiladi. Ma’no hozirgi bo‘lsa ham, shakl o‘tgan. ‘Would’ ham shunday: ‘I would suggest’. O‘zbekchadagi ‘so‘ramoqchi edim’ shunga juda yaxshi mos keladi.
scenes.say: Past and continuous forms create polite distance. I was wondering if you could help. We were thinking of moving the meeting. I would suggest a short break.
scenes.say_uz: O‘tgan va davomiy shakllar muloyim masofa yaratadi. Yordam bera olarmikansiz, deb o‘ylagandim. Uchrashuvni ko‘chirishni o‘ylayotgan edik. Qisqa tanaffus qilishni taklif qilgan bo‘lardim.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: zaif shakllar va ohang
board: I was wondering /aɪ wəz ˈwʌndərɪŋ/
Could you… /kʊdʒu/ · Would you… /wʊdʒu/
Fall-rise: Well… ↘↗ (reservation)
scenes.say_native: Talaffuz nuqtasi. Yumshatuvchi iboralar tez va zaif aytiladi: ‘was’ /wəz/, ‘could you’ birikib /kʊdʒu/ eshitiladi. Agar har bir so‘zni urg‘u bilan aytsangiz, nazokat yo‘qoladi va gap hatto kinoyali eshitilishi mumkin. Ohang ham muhim: ‘Well…’ so‘zida pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang e’tiroz borligini muloyim bildiradi.
scenes.say: I was wondering if you could help. Could you send it today? Notice the weak forms. And listen to the reservation in this: Well, it's an interesting idea.
scenes.say_uz: Yordam bera olarmikansiz. Bugun yubora olasizmi? Zaif shakllarga e’tibor bering. Bunda shubhani tinglang: Xo‘sh, qiziq g‘oya.

scenes.title: Keskin gaplar
board: ✗ You are wrong.
✓ I'm not sure that's entirely right.
✗ This idea is bad.
✓ I have a few reservations about this idea.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek o‘quvchilari ko‘pincha ‘You are wrong’ yoki ‘This idea is bad’ deydi. O‘zbekchada ‘bu noto‘g‘ri’ deyish iliq ohang bilan normal bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin inglizcha ish muhitida bu hujumdek eshitiladi. To‘g‘risi: ‘I’m not sure that’s entirely right’ yoki ‘I have a few reservations about this idea’. Fikr bir xil, ta’sir butunlay boshqa.
scenes.say: Not, you are wrong, but, I'm not sure that's entirely right. Not, this idea is bad, but, I have a few reservations about it.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Siz noto‘g‘risiz’ emas, ‘bu to‘liq to‘g‘ri ekaniga ishonchim yo‘q’. ‘Bu g‘oya yomon’ emas, ‘bu haqda ba’zi e’tirozlarim bor’.

scenes.title: Yumshating
board: 1) This plan is bad.
2) Your figures are wrong.
3) We need more time.
4) That's too expensive.
scenes.say_native: Navbat sizda. To‘rtta keskin gap. Har birini kamida ikkita vosita bilan yumshating: modal fe’l, yumshatuvchi so‘z, inkor plus ijobiy sifat yoki o‘tgan zamon. Ovoz chiqarib ayting va zaif shakllarga e’tibor bering. Bir gapni bir necha usulda yumshatib ko‘rsangiz, yanada yaxshi.
scenes.say: Soften these. This plan is bad. Your figures are wrong. We need more time. That's too expensive.
scenes.say_uz: Bularni yumshating. Bu reja yomon. Raqamlaringiz noto‘g‘ri. Bizga ko‘proq vaqt kerak. Bu juda qimmat.

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1) I'm not sure this plan is quite ready yet.
2) There may be a small error in the figures.
3) We might need a little more time.
4) It's slightly above our budget.
scenes.say_native: Namuna javoblar. Birinchi: ‘I’m not sure this plan is quite ready yet.’ Ikkinchi: ‘There may be a small error in the figures’, bu yerda ‘you’ ham olib tashlandi. Uchinchi: ‘We might need a little more time.’ To‘rtinchi: ‘It’s slightly above our budget.’ Sizning variantingiz boshqacha bo‘lishi mumkin, asosiysi ikki vosita ishlatilgan bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: I'm not sure this plan is quite ready yet. There may be a small error in the figures. We might need a little more time. It's slightly above our budget.
scenes.say_uz: Bu reja hali tayyor ekaniga ishonchim yo‘q. Raqamlarda kichik xato bo‘lishi mumkin. Bizga biroz ko‘proq vaqt kerak bo‘lishi mumkin. Bu byudjetimizdan biroz yuqori.

scenes.title: Haddan tashqari yumshatish
board: ✗ I would perhaps possibly maybe suggest…
✓ I'd suggest…
One or two softeners are enough
scenes.say_native: Teskari xato ham bor: yumshatuvchilarni ustma-ust qo‘yish. ‘I would perhaps possibly maybe suggest’ ishonchsiz va tushunarsiz eshitiladi, tinglovchi sizning asl fikringizni topa olmaydi. Bitta yoki ikkita vosita yetarli: ‘I’d suggest’. C2 darajasi ko‘p yumshatish emas, aniq dozalash demakdir.
scenes.say: Don't stack softeners. I would perhaps possibly maybe suggest sounds nervous. I'd suggest is polite and clear.
scenes.say_uz: Yumshatuvchilarni ustma-ust qo‘ymang. Juda ko‘p ehtiyotkorlik asabiy eshitiladi. ‘Taklif qilardim’ ham muloyim, ham aniq.

scenes.title: Iltimos zinapoyasi
board: Can you…? → Could you…?
Would you mind + -ing…?
I was wondering if you could…
Would it be possible to…?

examples.t: Would you mind sending it again?

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu: bilvosita iltimoslar. Ular zinapoyaga o‘xshaydi: ‘Can you’, keyin ‘Could you’, keyin ‘Would you mind’ va ‘-ing’, keyin ‘I was wondering if you could’, eng yuqorida ‘Would it be possible to’. Iltimos qanchalik katta bo‘lsa, shuncha yuqori pog‘onani tanlang. Kichik iltimos uchun eng yuqori pog‘ona esa kinoyali eshitilishi mumkin.
scenes.say: Could you check this? Would you mind checking this? I was wondering if you could check this. Would it be possible to check this before Friday?
scenes.say_uz: Buni tekshira olasizmi? Buni tekshirsangiz, malol kelmaydimi? Buni tekshira olarmikansiz, deb o‘ylagandim. Buni jumagacha tekshirishning iloji bormi?

scenes.title: Iltimosdagi grammatik xatolar
board: ✗ Would you mind to send it? → ✓ sending
✗ Could you tell me when is the meeting?
✓ Could you tell me when the meeting is?
Would you mind…? — No, not at all. (= Yes!)
scenes.say_native: Uchta xato. Birinchi: ‘would you mind’ dan keyin ‘-ing’ keladi, ‘to’ emas: ‘sending’. Ikkinchi: bilvosita savolda so‘z tartibi darak gapdagidek: ‘when the meeting is’, ‘when is the meeting’ emas. Uchinchi: ‘Would you mind?’ ga rozilik ‘No, not at all’, ya’ni ‘yo‘q, malol kelmaydi’. ‘Yes’ desangiz, aslida rad qilgan bo‘lasiz.
scenes.say: Would you mind sending it? Could you tell me when the meeting is? And if you agree, the answer is: No, not at all.
scenes.say_uz: Uni yuborsangiz, malol kelmaydimi? Uchrashuv qachonligini ayta olasizmi? Rozi bo‘lsangiz, javob: Yo‘q, aslo.

scenes.title: Bilvosita iltimos qiling
board: 1) Send me the file today.
2) Move the meeting to Thursday.
3) When does the train leave? (to a stranger)
scenes.say_native: Uchta to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gap. Har birini bilvosita iltimosga aylantiring. Birinchisi hamkasbga, ikkinchisi rahbaringizga, uchinchisi notanish odamga. Zinapoyadan to‘g‘ri pog‘onani tanlang va uchinchisida so‘z tartibiga ehtiyot bo‘ling. Iltimosning hajmini va suhbatdoshni hisobga oling.
scenes.say: Make these indirect. Send me the file today. Move the meeting to Thursday. And to a stranger: when does the train leave?
scenes.say_uz: Bularni bilvosita qiling. Faylni bugun yuboring. Uchrashuvni payshanbaga ko‘chiring. Notanish odamga: poyezd qachon jo‘naydi?

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1) Could you send me the file today?
2) Would it be possible to move the meeting to Thursday?
3) Could you tell me when the train leaves?
scenes.say_native: Namuna. Hamkasbga: ‘Could you send me the file today?’ Rahbarga, kattaroq iltimos bo‘lgani uchun: ‘Would it be possible to move the meeting to Thursday?’ Notanish odamga: ‘Excuse me, could you tell me when the train leaves?’ Uchinchisida ‘does’ yo‘qoldi va fe’l ‘leaves’ shaklini oldi. Bu juda ko‘p uchraydigan xato edi.
scenes.say: Could you send me the file today? Would it be possible to move the meeting to Thursday? Excuse me, could you tell me when the train leaves?
scenes.say_uz: Faylni bugun yubora olasizmi? Uchrashuvni payshanbaga ko‘chirishning iloji bormi? Kechirasiz, poyezd qachon jo‘nashini ayta olasizmi?

scenes.title: Rad javobi tuzilishi
board: 1) Appreciate: Thanks for thinking of me.
2) Regret: I'm afraid…
3) Reason: I'm fully committed until May.
4) Alternative: Could I help next month?

examples.t: I'm afraid I can't make it on Friday.

scenes.say_native: Endi rad javobi. Diplomatik ‘yo‘q’ to‘rt qismdan iborat: minnatdorlik, afsus, sabab va muqobil. ‘Thanks for thinking of me. I’m afraid I’m fully committed until May. Could I help next month instead?’ ‘I’m afraid’ bu yerda qo‘rqish emas, ‘afsuski’ degani. Muqobil taklif munosabatni saqlaydi.
scenes.say: Thanks for thinking of me. I'm afraid I'm fully committed until May. Could I help next month instead?
scenes.say_uz: Meni eslaganingiz uchun rahmat. Afsuski, mayga qadar to‘liq bandman. O‘rniga keyingi oy yordam bersam bo‘ladimi?

scenes.title: ‘No’ demay yo‘q deyish
board: That might be a bit tricky.
Let me get back to you on that.
It's not really my area.
I'll see what I can do. (often: probably not)
scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida ko‘pincha ‘no’ so‘zi umuman aytilmaydi. ‘That might be a bit tricky’ odatda ‘bu qiyin, ehtimol bo‘lmaydi’ degani. ‘Let me get back to you’ vaqt yutadi. ‘It’s not really my area’ mas’uliyatni to‘g‘ri odamga yo‘naltiradi. ‘I’ll see what I can do’ ba’zan haqiqiy va’da, ba’zan muloyim rad. Ohang va kontekstga qarab farqlang.
scenes.say: That might be a bit tricky usually means no. Let me get back to you buys time. And I'll see what I can do can be a real promise or a polite no.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Bu biroz qiyin bo‘lishi mumkin’ odatda yo‘q degani. ‘Sizga keyinroq javob beray’ vaqt yutadi. ‘Nima qila olishimni ko‘raman’ haqiqiy va’da ham, muloyim rad ham bo‘lishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Tinglash: qo‘shimcha loyiha
board: Dialogue: a manager and a colleague
Listen for: the refusal and the alternative
scenes.say_native: Birinchi tinglash. Rahbar Sara hamkasbi Tomga yangi loyihani taklif qilyapti. Tom band va rad etishi kerak. U ‘no’ so‘zini ishlatadimi? Rad javobining to‘rt qismini topishga harakat qiling: minnatdorlik, afsus, sabab va muqobil. Tom buni qanday qilganini kuzating.
scenes.say: Sara: Tom, I was wondering if you'd be able to lead the new client project. Tom: Thank you, I'm flattered you thought of me. I'm afraid my plate is rather full at the moment, with the audit running until June. Sara: I see. It is quite urgent. Tom: I understand. Would it help if I mentored whoever takes it on? I could spend an hour a week with them. Sara: That would actually be very useful. Let me think about who might lead it.
scenes.say_uz: Sara: Tom, yangi mijoz loyihasiga rahbarlik qila olarmikansiz, deb o‘ylagandim. Tom: Rahmat, meni eslaganingizdan xursandman. Afsuski, hozir ishim ancha ko‘p, audit iyungacha davom etadi. Sara: Tushunarli. Bu ancha shoshilinch. Tom: Tushunaman. Kim olsa, unga murabbiylik qilsam yordam beradimi? Haftasiga bir soat ajrata olaman. Sara: Bu haqiqatan juda foydali bo‘lardi. Kim boshqarishi mumkinligini o‘ylab ko‘ray.

scenes.title: Suhbatni tahlil qiling
board: 1) How does Sara make her request?
2) What reason does Tom give?
3) What alternative does he offer?
4) Does he ever say 'no'?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Sara iltimosini qanday shaklda aytdi? Tom qanday sabab keltirdi? U qanday muqobil taklif qildi? Va Tom biror marta ‘no’ so‘zini aytdimi? Javoblarni inglizcha, imkon qadar suhbatdagi iboralar bilan ayting. Kerak bo‘lsa, suhbatni xayolan qayta eslang.
scenes.say: How does Sara make her request? What reason does Tom give? What alternative does he offer? Does he ever say no?
scenes.say_uz: Sara iltimosini qanday aytadi? Tom qanday sabab keltiradi? U qanday muqobil taklif qiladi? U biror marta ‘yo‘q’ deydimi?

scenes.title: Suhbat javoblari
board: 1) I was wondering if you'd be able to…
2) My plate is rather full: the audit until June.
3) Mentoring the new leader, an hour a week
4) No — the refusal is implied
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Sara ‘I was wondering if you’d be able to’ dedi, zinapoyaning yuqori pog‘onasi. Tomning sababi: ‘my plate is rather full’, ya’ni ishim ko‘p, audit iyungacha. Muqobil: yangi rahbarga haftasiga bir soat murabbiylik. Va ‘no’ so‘zi umuman aytilmadi, lekin rad aniq tushunildi. Bu diplomatiyaning eng yaxshi namunasi.
scenes.say: Sara used I was wondering. Tom said his plate was rather full. He offered to mentor the new leader. And he never said no, yet the refusal was perfectly clear.
scenes.say_uz: Sara ‘I was wondering’ dedi. Tom ishi ko‘pligini aytdi. U yangi rahbarga murabbiylik qilishni taklif qildi. U hech qachon ‘yo‘q’ demadi, lekin rad aniq edi.

scenes.title: Diplomatik rad eting
board: 1) A colleague: Can you cover my shift on Saturday?
2) A client: Can you give us a 30% discount?
Use: appreciate + regret + reason + alternative
scenes.say_native: Endi o‘zingiz rad eting. Birinchi vaziyat: hamkasbingiz shanba kungi smenasini almashtirib berishingizni so‘rayapti. Ikkinchi: mijoz o‘ttiz foiz chegirma so‘rayapti. To‘rt qismli tuzilmani ishlating va ‘no’ so‘zisiz javob bering. Javobingiz qisqa, lekin iliq bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Refuse politely. A colleague asks: can you cover my shift on Saturday? A client asks: can you give us a thirty per cent discount?
scenes.say_uz: Muloyim rad eting. Hamkasb so‘raydi: shanba kuni smenamni almashtirib bera olasizmi? Mijoz so‘raydi: bizga o‘ttiz foiz chegirma bera olasizmi?

scenes.title: Namuna rad javoblari
board: 1) I'd love to help, but I'm away this weekend. Could you ask Ali?
2) I'm afraid 30% wouldn't be possible.
We could look at 10% for a longer contract.
scenes.say_native: Namuna. Hamkasbga: ‘I’d love to help, but I’m away this weekend. Have you tried asking Ali?’ Mijozga: ‘I’m afraid thirty per cent wouldn’t be possible. We could, however, look at ten per cent for a longer contract.’ Ikkinchisida ‘wouldn’t’ shartli shakli rad javobini yumshatdi, muqobil esa muzokarani davom ettirdi.
scenes.say: I'd love to help, but I'm away this weekend. Have you tried asking Ali? I'm afraid thirty per cent wouldn't be possible. We could, however, look at ten per cent for a longer contract.
scenes.say_uz: Yordam bergim keladi, lekin bu dam olish kunlari yo‘qman. Alidan so‘rab ko‘rdingizmi? Afsuski, o‘ttiz foizning iloji bo‘lmaydi. Ammo uzoqroq shartnoma uchun o‘n foizni ko‘rib chiqishimiz mumkin.

scenes.title: Obro‘ (face) tushunchasi
board: Face = public self-image
Positive face: to be liked and respected
Negative face: not to be imposed on
scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: obro‘ni saqlash. Tilshunoslar Brown va Levinson ‘face’, ya’ni jamoat oldidagi obro‘ tushunchasini rivojlantirgan. Har bir odam yoqishni va hurmat qilinishni xohlaydi, shu bilan birga, unga majburiyat yuklanmasligini istaydi. O‘zbek madaniyatida ‘yuzini yerga qaratmaslik’ degan tushuncha bor, bu ingliz tilidagi ‘save face’ ga juda yaqin.
scenes.say: Everyone has face: a wish to be liked and respected, and a wish not to be imposed on. Diplomatic language protects both.
scenes.say_uz: Har kimning obro‘si bor: yoqish va hurmat qilinish istagi hamda o‘ziga majburiyat yuklanmaslik istagi. Diplomatik til ikkalasini ham himoya qiladi.

scenes.title: Shaxssiz qilish
board: You missed the deadline. → The deadline was missed.
You made an error. → There seems to be an error.
you → we: We need to look at this again.

examples.t: There seems to be a discrepancy in the figures.

scenes.say_native: Obro‘ni saqlashning eng kuchli vositasi: ‘you’ ni olib tashlash. Majhul nisbat: ‘The deadline was missed’. ‘There seems to be’ tuzilmasi: ‘There seems to be a discrepancy in the figures.’ Yoki ‘you’ o‘rniga ‘we’: ‘We need to look at this again.’ Muammo aytiladi, lekin barmoq bilan bir odamga ko‘rsatilmaydi.
scenes.say: Remove the you. The deadline was missed. There seems to be a discrepancy in the figures. We need to look at this again.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Siz’ ni olib tashlang. Muddat o‘tkazib yuborildi. Raqamlarda nomuvofiqlik borga o‘xshaydi. Buni qayta ko‘rib chiqishimiz kerak.

scenes.title: Boshqaning va o‘zingizning obro‘yingiz
board: Their face: It's an easy mistake to make.
I may not have explained it clearly.
Your face: On reflection, I may have been too hasty.
Fair point. · I take your point.
scenes.say_native: Boshqaning obro‘sini saqlash uchun aybni yumshating yoki o‘zingizga oling: ‘It’s an easy mistake to make’, ‘I may not have explained it clearly.’ O‘z xatoingizni esa nafis tan oling: ‘On reflection, I may have been too hasty’, ‘Fair point’, ‘I take your point.’ Xatoni chiroyli tan olish zaiflik emas, C2 darajasidagi ishonch belgisi.
scenes.say: It's an easy mistake to make. I may not have explained it clearly. And for yourself: on reflection, I may have been a little hasty. Fair point.
scenes.say_uz: Bu oson qilinadigan xato. Ehtimol, men aniq tushuntirmaganman. O‘zingiz uchun: o‘ylab ko‘rsam, biroz shoshilgan bo‘lsam kerak. To‘g‘ri gap.

scenes.title: ‘You’ bilan ayblash
board: ✗ You made a mistake in the figures.
✓ There seems to be an error in the figures.
✗ You didn't understand me.
✓ I may not have been clear.
scenes.say_native: Tipik xato: muammoni ‘you’ bilan boshlash. ‘You made a mistake’, ‘You didn’t understand me’ ayblovdek eshitiladi va suhbatdosh darhol himoyaga o‘tadi. To‘g‘risi: ‘There seems to be an error’, ‘I may not have been clear.’ Ikkinchisida mas’uliyatni o‘zingizga olasiz, garchi xato boshqada bo‘lsa ham. Bu muloqotni saqlab qoladi.
scenes.say: Not, you made a mistake, but, there seems to be an error. Not, you didn't understand me, but, I may not have been clear.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Siz xato qildingiz’ emas, ‘xato borga o‘xshaydi’. ‘Siz meni tushunmadingiz’ emas, ‘ehtimol, men aniq gapirmaganman’.

scenes.title: Obro‘ni saqlang
board: 1) You forgot to send the invoice.
2) You're late again.
3) You misread the brief.
4) I was wrong. (say it gracefully)
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Birinchi uchtasida ‘you’ ni olib tashlang: majhul nisbat, ‘there seems to be’ yoki ‘we’ dan foydalaning. To‘rtinchisida o‘z xatoingizni nafis tan oling. Har birini ovoz chiqarib, muloyim ohangda ayting. ‘Again’ so‘ziga alohida e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Rephrase these. You forgot to send the invoice. You're late again. You misread the brief. And say gracefully: I was wrong.
scenes.say_uz: Qayta tuzing. Hisob-fakturani yuborishni unutdingiz. Yana kechikdingiz. Topshiriqni noto‘g‘ri tushundingiz. Nafis ayting: men xato qildim.

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1) The invoice doesn't seem to have gone out yet.
2) We seem to be starting a bit late again.
3) There may have been a misunderstanding about the brief.
4) On reflection, I think you were right.
scenes.say_native: Namuna. ‘The invoice doesn’t seem to have gone out yet.’ ‘We seem to be starting a bit late again’, bu yerda ‘we’ ayblovni umumiy qildi. ‘There may have been a misunderstanding about the brief.’ Va o‘zingiz uchun: ‘On reflection, I think you were right.’ To‘rttasida ham muammo aniq aytildi, lekin hech kim kamsitilmadi.
scenes.say: The invoice doesn't seem to have gone out yet. We seem to be starting a bit late again. There may have been a misunderstanding about the brief. On reflection, I think you were right.
scenes.say_uz: Hisob-faktura hali yuborilmaganga o‘xshaydi. Yana biroz kech boshlayotganga o‘xshaymiz. Topshiriq bo‘yicha tushunmovchilik bo‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkin. O‘ylab ko‘rsam, siz haq edingiz.

scenes.title: Diplomatik tanqid tuzilishi
board: 1) Positive: The structure works really well.
2) Concern: My only concern is the length.
3) Suggestion: Perhaps we could cut section 3?

examples.t: My only concern is the length.

scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: diplomatik tanqid. Uch qadam: aniq ijobiy fikr, bitta asosiy xavotir, konstruktiv taklif. ‘The structure works really well. My only concern is the length. Perhaps we could cut section three?’ ‘My only concern’ iborasi muammoni kichraytiradi va u yagona ekanini ko‘rsatadi. Ijobiy fikr esa aniq bo‘lishi kerak, umumiy ‘good’ emas.
scenes.say: The structure works really well. My only concern is the length. Perhaps we could cut section three?
scenes.say_uz: Tuzilish juda yaxshi ishlaydi. Meni faqat hajmi o‘ylantiradi. Balki uchinchi bo‘limni qisqartirarmiz?

scenes.title: Tanqid iboralari
board: It could be even stronger if…
One thing you might consider is…
Have you thought about…?
Wouldn't it be better to…? · Isn't there a risk that…?

examples.t: Isn't there a risk that clients will find it too long?
examples.uz: Mijozlar uni juda uzun deb topishi xavfi yo‘qmi?

scenes.say_native: Tanqidni taklif shaklida berish iboralari: ‘It could be even stronger if…’, ‘One thing you might consider is…’, ‘Have you thought about…?’. Inkor savollar ham juda diplomatik: ‘Wouldn’t it be better to…?’, ‘Isn’t there a risk that…?’ Ular suhbatdoshni xulosaga o‘zi kelishga undaydi. O‘zbekchadagi ‘…sa yaxshi bo‘lmasmidi?’ shunga o‘xshaydi.
scenes.say: It could be even stronger if you added a case study. Have you thought about a shorter version? Wouldn't it be better to start with the results?
scenes.say_uz: Agar amaliy misol qo‘shsangiz, yanada kuchliroq bo‘lardi. Qisqaroq variant haqida o‘ylab ko‘rdingizmi? Natijalardan boshlash yaxshiroq bo‘lmasmidi?

scenes.title: Britaniya understatementini tushunish
board: That's an interesting idea. (often: I doubt it)
With the greatest respect… (= I strongly disagree)
I hear what you say. (= I disagree)
Not bad at all. (= very good)
scenes.say_native: Diplomatik tilni nafaqat gapirish, balki tushunish ham kerak. Britaniya nutqida ‘That’s an interesting idea’ ko‘pincha shubhani bildiradi. ‘With the greatest respect’ odatda kuchli e’tirozdan oldin keladi. ‘I hear what you say’ ko‘pincha ‘men rozi emasman’ degani. Teskarisi ham bor: ‘not bad at all’ ko‘pincha katta maqtov. Ohang va kontekstga qarang.
scenes.say: With the greatest respect usually comes before strong disagreement. I hear what you say often means I disagree. And not bad at all is often high praise.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Katta hurmat bilan’ odatda kuchli e’tirozdan oldin keladi. ‘Gapingizni eshityapman’ ko‘pincha ‘rozi emasman’ degani. ‘Umuman yomon emas’ esa ko‘pincha katta maqtov.

scenes.title: Tinglash: taqdimot bo‘yicha fikr
board: Dialogue: feedback on a presentation
Listen for: praise → concern → suggestion
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash. Rahbar Helen xodimi Jamesning taqdimotiga fikr bildiryapti. U tanqidni qanday tuzganiga e’tibor bering: avval nima deydi, xavotirini qaysi ibora bilan kiritadi va qanday taklif beradi. James tanqidga qanday munosabat bildiradi? Har bir iborani yozib oling.
scenes.say: Helen: James, the opening was genuinely engaging, and the client clearly liked the case study. James: Thanks, that's good to hear. Helen: My only real concern is the pricing slide. Isn't there a risk it raises more questions than it answers? James: Fair point. I did wonder about that. Helen: One thing you might consider is moving the detailed figures to an appendix. James: That makes sense. I'll rework it before Thursday.
scenes.say_uz: Helen: James, kirish qismi haqiqatan qiziqarli bo‘ldi, mijozga amaliy misol aniq yoqdi. James: Rahmat, buni eshitish yoqimli. Helen: Meni faqat narxlar slaydi o‘ylantiradi. U javob berganidan ko‘ra ko‘proq savol tug‘dirishi xavfi yo‘qmi? James: To‘g‘ri gap. Men ham bu haqda o‘ylagandim. Helen: Batafsil raqamlarni ilovaga ko‘chirishni ko‘rib chiqsangiz bo‘lardi. James: Mantiqli. Payshanbagacha qayta ishlab chiqaman.

scenes.title: Fikr-mulohazani tahlil qiling
board: 1) What two things does Helen praise?
2) How does she introduce the problem?
3) What does she suggest?
4) How does James accept the criticism?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Helen qaysi ikki narsani maqtadi? Muammoni qaysi ibora bilan kiritdi? Qanday taklif berdi? James tanqidni qaysi ibora bilan qabul qildi? Javob berishda suhbatdagi aniq iboralarni takrorlashga harakat qiling. Har bir javobni bitta qisqa gap bilan ayting.
scenes.say: What two things does Helen praise? How does she introduce the problem? What does she suggest? How does James accept the criticism?
scenes.say_uz: Helen qaysi ikki narsani maqtaydi? Muammoni qanday kiritadi? Nima taklif qiladi? James tanqidni qanday qabul qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1) the opening and the case study
2) My only real concern is… + Isn't there a risk…?
3) moving the figures to an appendix
4) Fair point. I did wonder about that.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Helen kirish qismini va amaliy misolni maqtadi, aniq va samimiy. Muammoni ‘My only real concern is’ bilan kiritdi va inkor savol berdi: ‘Isn’t there a risk…?’ Taklifi: raqamlarni ilovaga ko‘chirish, ‘One thing you might consider’ iborasi bilan. James esa ‘Fair point’ deb, obro‘sini saqlagan holda tanqidni qabul qildi.
scenes.say: She praised the opening and the case study. She used my only real concern and a negative question. She suggested an appendix. And James replied, fair point.
scenes.say_uz: U kirish va amaliy misolni maqtadi. ‘Meni faqat … o‘ylantiradi’ va inkor savoldan foydalandi. Ilovani taklif qildi. James esa ‘to‘g‘ri gap’ deb javob berdi.

scenes.title: ‘But’ maqtovni o‘chiradi
board: ✗ Great job, but the data is wrong.
✓ The structure works well. One thing to double-check is the data on slide 5.
✗ Good, but… (vague praise)
scenes.say_native: Tipik xato: ‘Great job, but…’. ‘But’ dan keyin tinglovchi oldingi maqtovni unutadi va faqat tanqidni eshitadi. Bundan tashqari, umumiy ‘good’ yoki ‘great job’ samimiy eshitilmaydi. Yaxshisi: aniq maqtov, keyin yangi gap bilan xavotir: ‘The structure works well. One thing to double-check is the data on slide five.’
scenes.say: Avoid great job, but. Try: the structure works well. One thing to double-check is the data on slide five.
scenes.say_uz: ‘Zo‘r, lekin’ dan qoching. Shunday deb ko‘ring: tuzilish yaxshi ishlaydi. Beshinchi slayddagi ma’lumotni qayta tekshirish kerak.

scenes.title: Diplomatik tanqid bering
board: 1) A colleague's report is far too long.
2) A team member talks over others in meetings.
3) A friend's business plan ignores competitors.
scenes.say_native: Uchta vaziyat. Har biri uchun uch qadamli tanqid tuzing: aniq ijobiy fikr, bitta xavotir va taklif. Kamida bitta inkor savol yoki ‘One thing you might consider’ kabi iborani ishlating. Ikkinchi vaziyat eng nozik, chunki u shaxsiy xulq haqida. Javobingiz aniq, lekin hurmatli bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Give diplomatic feedback. A colleague's report is far too long. A team member talks over others in meetings. A friend's business plan ignores competitors.
scenes.say_uz: Diplomatik fikr bildiring. Hamkasbning hisoboti juda uzun. Jamoa a’zosi yig‘ilishlarda boshqalarning gapini bo‘ladi. Do‘stning biznes-rejasi raqobatchilarni e’tiborsiz qoldiradi.

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1) The analysis is thorough. It could be even stronger if it were shorter.
2) I wonder if we could all make sure everyone finishes their point.
3) The idea is exciting. Have you thought about how competitors might react?
scenes.say_native: Namuna. Birinchi: ‘The analysis is really thorough. It could be even stronger if it were a bit shorter.’ Ikkinchi, xulq haqida, shuning uchun ‘we’ ishlatildi: ‘I wonder if we could all make sure everyone finishes their point.’ Uchinchi, savol shaklida: ‘The idea is exciting. Have you thought about how competitors might react?’
scenes.say: The analysis is really thorough. It could be even stronger if it were a bit shorter. I wonder if we could all make sure everyone finishes their point. The idea is exciting. Have you thought about how competitors might react?
scenes.say_uz: Tahlil juda puxta. Biroz qisqaroq bo‘lsa, yanada kuchliroq bo‘lardi. Har kim fikrini oxirigacha aytishiga hammamiz e’tibor bersak-chi. G‘oya qiziqarli. Raqobatchilar qanday javob berishi haqida o‘ylab ko‘rdingizmi?

scenes.title: Qachon to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gapirish kerak
board: Safety: Stop! Don't touch that.
Urgent instructions: Call an ambulance.
Diplomacy ≠ vagueness
scenes.say_native: Muhim chegara: diplomatiya har doim ham to‘g‘ri tanlov emas. Xavfsizlik, favqulodda holat va aniq ko‘rsatmalarda qisqa va to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gapiring: ‘Stop! Don’t touch that.’ Shuningdek, juda muhim xavfni haddan tashqari yumshatsangiz, tinglovchi uni sezmay qolishi mumkin. Diplomatiya noaniqlik emas: xabar baribir aniq yetib borishi kerak.
scenes.say: In an emergency, be direct: stop, don't touch that. Diplomacy is never an excuse for vagueness; the message must still arrive.
scenes.say_uz: Favqulodda holatda to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gapiring: to‘xtang, unga tegmang. Diplomatiya hech qachon noaniqlikka bahona emas; xabar baribir yetib borishi kerak.

scenes.title: Yakuniy rolli o‘yin
board: Your manager wants the project finished in one week.
You think it needs three.
Speak for 45–60 seconds: hedge, refuse, propose.
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy og‘zaki topshiriq. Rahbaringiz loyihani bir haftada tugatishni xohlaydi, siz esa uch hafta kerak deb hisoblaysiz. Qirq besh soniyadan bir daqiqagacha gapiring: minnatdorlik, yumshatilgan e’tiroz, sabab va muqobil taklif. Kamida bitta o‘tgan zamonli iltimos va bitta inkor savol ishlating.
scenes.say: Your manager wants the project finished in one week, but you believe it needs three. Respond diplomatically in about a minute.
scenes.say_uz: Rahbaringiz loyihani bir haftada tugatishni xohlaydi, lekin siz uch hafta kerak deb hisoblaysiz. Taxminan bir daqiqada diplomatik javob bering.

scenes.title: Namuna javob
board: I appreciate the urgency…
I'm not sure one week is quite realistic…
Wouldn't it be safer to…?
I was wondering if we could…
scenes.say_native: Namunani tinglang va o‘zingiznikiga solishtiring. Unda minnatdorlik bor, e’tiroz yumshatilgan, sabab aniq, inkor savol bor va oxirida aniq muqobil taklif qilinadi. E’tibor bering: muloyimlikka qaramay, ‘bir hafta yetmaydi’ degan xabar to‘liq yetib boradi. Diplomatiya shu degani.
scenes.say: I appreciate the urgency, and I can see why the client wants it quickly. I'm just not sure one week is quite realistic, given the testing involved. Wouldn't it be safer to deliver the core features first? I was wondering if we could agree on one week for those, and two more for the rest.
scenes.say_uz: Shoshilinchlikni tushunaman va mijoz nega tez olishni xohlashini ko‘ryapman. Faqat sinovlarni hisobga olsak, bir hafta real ekaniga ishonchim yo‘q. Avval asosiy funksiyalarni topshirish xavfsizroq emasmi? Ular uchun bir hafta, qolgani uchun yana ikki hafta kelishib olsak bo‘larmikin, deb o‘ylagandim.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
board: 1) Hedging: might, seem, a bit, not ideal, I was wondering
2) Indirect requests & refusals
3) Face-saving: remove 'you', admit gracefully
4) Criticism: praise → concern → suggestion
scenes.say_native: Qisqacha takrorlaymiz. Birinchi: hedging va yumshatish: modal fe’llar, seem, a bit, not ideal, o‘tgan zamon. Ikkinchi: iltimos zinapoyasi va to‘rt qismli rad javobi. Uchinchi: obro‘ni saqlash: ‘you’ ni olib tashlash va xatoni nafis tan olish. To‘rtinchi: diplomatik tanqid: aniq maqtov, bitta xavotir, taklif. Va eslang: diplomatiya noaniqlik emas.
scenes.say: Hedge with modals and softeners. Climb the request ladder. Refuse with thanks, regret, reason and an alternative. Protect face. And criticise with praise, one concern and a suggestion.
scenes.say_uz: Modal fe’llar va yumshatuvchilar bilan ehtiyotkor gapiring. Iltimos zinapoyasidan foydalaning. Minnatdorlik, afsus, sabab va muqobil bilan rad eting. Obro‘ni saqlang. Maqtov, bitta xavotir va taklif bilan tanqid qiling.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: rewrite 8 direct statements diplomatically
Use at least 2 techniques in each
Next: developing topics in depth
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘zingiz ish yoki o‘qishda eshitadigan sakkizta keskin gapni yozing va har birini diplomatik shaklga keltiring. Har birida kamida ikkita vosita bo‘lsin, va ularni nomlang: masalan, modal fe’l va ‘you’ ni olib tashlash. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: sakkiztasi ham muloyim, lekin asl xabari aniq saqlangan. Keyingi darsda mavzuni chuqur rivojlantirishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Rewrite eight direct statements diplomatically, using at least two techniques in each. Next time, we learn to develop a topic in real depth.
scenes.say_uz: Sakkizta keskin gapni diplomatik qayta yozing, har birida kamida ikkita usuldan foydalaning. Keyingi safar mavzuni chuqur rivojlantirishni o‘rganamiz.

homework_uz: Ish yoki o‘qishda eshitadigan sakkizta to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri, keskin gapni yozing va har birini diplomatik shaklda qayta tuzing. Har bir gapda kamida ikkita vositani ishlating (modal fe’l, yumshatuvchi so‘z, o‘tgan zamonli iltimos, ‘you’ ni olib tashlash, inkor savol va hokazo) va ularni nomlang. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: sakkizta gapning hammasi muloyim, grammatik jihatdan to‘g‘ri va asl xabari aniq saqlangan.

quiz.q: Which is the most diplomatic way to disagree?
options: I'm not sure that's entirely right.
quiz.why_uz: ‘Not sure’ va ‘entirely’ fikrni yumshatadi; qolganlari keskin eshitiladi.
Would you mind dan keyin -ing shakli keladi; ‘to close’ — keng tarqalgan xato.

options: Could you tell me where is the station?
Could you tell me where the station is?
Could you tell me where does the station is?
Could you tell me where the station it is?
quiz.why_uz: Bilvosita savolda so‘z tartibi darak gapdagidek: where the station is.

quiz.q: Someone asks 'Would you mind if I sat here?' You agree. What do you say?
quiz.why_uz: Mind — malol kelmoq; rozilik ‘No, not at all’ bilan bildiriladi.

quiz.q: Which sentence uses tense to soften a request?
options: I was wondering if you could help.
I will wonder if you can help.
quiz.why_uz: O‘tgan davomiy ‘I was wondering’ hozirgi iltimosni muloyim qiladi.

quiz.q: Which is the most face-saving way to point out an error?
options: There seems to be an error in the figures.
Why did you do this wrong?
quiz.why_uz: ‘There seems to be’ ‘you’ ni olib tashlaydi va ayblovni yumshatadi.

quiz.q: In British English, 'With the greatest respect…' usually signals…
quiz.why_uz: Bu ibora ko‘pincha kuchli e’tirozdan oldin keladi.

quiz.q: Which is the best diplomatic refusal?
options: Thanks for asking. I'm afraid I'm fully booked, but I could help next week.
quiz.why_uz: Minnatdorlik, afsus, sabab va muqobil — to‘liq diplomatik rad javobi.

quiz.q: What is wrong with 'I would perhaps possibly maybe suggest a change'?
options: Too many softeners make it sound unclear.
quiz.why_uz: Yumshatuvchilarni ustma-ust qo‘yish ishonchsiz va noaniq eshitiladi.

quiz.q: Which phrase introduces criticism as a suggestion?
options: One thing you might consider is…
quiz.why_uz: ‘One thing you might consider’ tanqidni taklif shakliga keltiradi.
